question: Which components improve held-out control quality per actual training second?

conditions.hypothesis: Fewer optimizer passes increase useful experience per second enough to retain or improve validation distance.
Removing stacked history changes control quality and training cost; current-frame velocities and previous pedals remain available.
Training with dynamics perturbations improves zero-shot held-out vehicle performance, potentially reducing source-map quality.

controls: Each run starts with fresh weights and no parent checkpoint.
Compare complete configurations under equal actual wall-clock budgets; initialization and checkpoint overhead are counted.
Use the same seed set, source version, machine, evaluation horizon and held-out validation seeds.
Run conditions sequentially; randomize condition order within each training seed and record the realized order.
Do not run performance trials concurrently with the governed one-hour session.
decision_rule: Treat validation quality, variability and runtime jointly. Preserve unfavorable results. Three seeds are exploratory and do not justify broad statistical superiority claims.
scope_limit: This factorial component screen does not establish pixel perception, calibrated dynamics or real-game transfer.
